key_insight: T2I models and current evaluators prefer visually vivid, over-saturated images; this paper provides a benchmark and calibration methods to quantify and correct color fidelity so generated images better match real-world photographic color distributions.
problem_solved: Addresses the bias in generation and evaluation that rewards exaggerated saturation/contrast—making outputs look "too vivid to be real"—by creating tools to measure, compare, and calibrate color realism across models.
method: Assemble a benchmark and evaluation protocol that pairs real photographs with prompts and computes color-fidelity statistics between real and generated sets.
Define objective color-fidelity metrics (distributional comparisons, perceptual color-difference measures) to reveal vividness bias in human ratings and learned metrics.
Provide a calibration pipeline (post-hoc color-distribution alignment, color-aware loss or fine-tuning strategies) to adjust generated images toward photographic color statistics.
impact: Gives researchers and practitioners a practical way to detect and correct color biases, improving realism for photographic-style T2I outputs and enabling fairer model comparisons and evaluation practices.
visual_elements: Before/after image pairs showing typical over-saturated generation vs. calibrated (photographic) output.
Overlaid color histograms or 2D chromaticity plots comparing real vs. generated distributions.
Bar/line chart of color-fidelity metric scores across multiple SOTA models, highlighting vividness bias.
Flow diagram of the benchmark → metric → calibration pipeline (data, evaluation, correction steps).
paper_title: Too Vivid to Be Real? Benchmarking and Calibrating Generative Color Fidelity
paper_authors: Zhengyao Fang, Zexi Jia, Yijia Zhong, Pengcheng Luo, Jinchao Zhang
